text:
sana: hi all, onboarding snag. when I try to clone git@github.com:redwood/inference-templates.git I get a 403 in the web UI and a message that SAML SSO is required. I accepted the org invite but the repo is private. any tips?
leo: welcome Sana! git clone failing with a SAML message usually means you need to "Authorize with SSO" on your GitHub account for the org. go to https://github.com/organizations/redwood-inference/settings/sso or check your profile -> Organizations -> Redwood Inference and click "Authorize".
sana: I don't see the authorize button, just "You are a member" and the repo still 403s in the browser.
itops: ops-bot shows SCIM provision completed for sana@redwood.com at 2025-05-12T09:03Z. ops-bot: "SCIM: user provisioned -> teams: platform, infra". can you confirm which email you accepted with? SAML ties to the org account.
sana: accepted invite on my work email (sana@redwood.com). i also tried logging into the web UI and forcing a new session.
maria: if the SAML session isn't authorized, GH will block access to private repos until you click the org's SSO authorization flow. sometimes the button is tucked under the org card. steps: Profile > Organizations > click the org > there should be a blue "Authorize" button that pops a consent dialog for SSO.
sana: found it! clicked authorize, it asked to connect my Okta session. clicked allow. still can't clone from terminal: git clone returns "remote: Repository not found."
leo: after authorizing SSO you might need to re-authenticate your local git/gh session. what method are you using — ssh or HTTPS?
sana: ssh (I added my key earlier). `git clone git@github.com:redwood/inference-templates.git` -> "remote: Repository not found."
itops: try `ssh -T git@github.com` to verify SSH auth. also check your SSH key is associated with your org account and not added mistakenly as a deploy key on some repo.
sana: `ssh -T git@github.com` -> "Hi sanaredwood! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access." so SSH auth looks fine.
leo: ok SSH is fine. "Repository not found" after SSO usually means your org-level SAML authorization isn't applied to your SSH key yet. Go to https://github.com/settings/sessions and click "Authorize SAML" for Redwood Inference if it appears. Also try `gh auth status` and `gh auth refresh -h github.com` to refresh GitHub CLI tokens, which can update HTTPS auth.
sana: ran `gh auth status` -> shows logged in with 'sana@redwood.com' but no SSO token. ran `gh auth refresh -h github.com` and it opened a browser, completed SSO.
ops-bot: "SCIM: refreshed membership for user sana@redwood.com"
sana: cloning now... `git clone git@github.com:redwood/inference-templates.git` -> cloning in progress...
sana: clone finished! :party: I also couldn't see some private repo listings until I flipped the SSO authorize switch. thanks.
maria: great — leaving a note on the onboarding checklist: ensure new hires get the "Authorize SSO" reminder in the welcome doc and we should prefer sending invites to the redwood.com email only.
leo: small FYI: if you ever switch between personal and work accounts in the same browser, SSO prompts can get confused. incognito or try `gh auth logout` then `gh auth login --web` if you hit it again.
itops: adding a ticket to ops backlog to add SSO step to the new-hires flow. welcome again, @sana :wave:
